title: Storm Soaks the Northeast: 100,000 Lose Power
summary: Imagine looking at your phone and seeing water rising inside your own business. That's what Kenny Formica did on Saturday. He owns Surf City Marina on the Jersey Shore, and cameras showed water creeping into his building. He said that almost never happens — the last time was Hurricane Sandy, which caused more than $4 million in damage. This storm is called a nor'easter (a big storm that forms along the East Coast). It is moving very slowly, so it stays in one area for a long time. About 100,000 customers in the Northeast lost power. Tens of millions of people were in its path. In Edgewater, New Jersey, water filled a parking lot, and one car was almost underwater — only its sunroof stuck out. Hundreds of flights were cancelled at Boston Logan Airport. The Boston Red Sox even moved a game all the way to Florida to avoid the rain. Forecasters say more wind, rain and high tides are coming. "Mark my words: Much more is coming," said New York Gov. Kathy Hochul.
why_it_matters: Storms like this show how weather can suddenly close schools, cancel plans and knock out the power at home, which is why families keep flashlights and extra water ready.

background_read: A nor'easter is a storm that forms along the East Coast of the United States, usually in fall or winter, when cold air over the land meets warm, wet air over the ocean.
Hurricane Sandy (a giant storm that flooded the New Jersey and New York coast in 2012) is still remembered there as one of the worst storms ever.

The Northeast is the group of states in the top-right corner of the country — New York, New Jersey and Massachusetts are some of them — and Boston Logan Airport (a big airport in Boston) is one of the busiest in that region.
Article_Structure: WHO: Kenny Formica, who owns Surf City Marina on the Jersey Shore, about 100,000 customers who lost power, and New York Gov. Kathy Hochul.
WHAT: A slow-moving nor'easter soaked the Northeast, flooded streets and buildings, cancelled hundreds of flights and knocked out power.
WHERE: The Northeast United States — the Jersey Shore, Edgewater in New Jersey, and Boston, Massachusetts.
WHY: The storm formed along the East Coast and moved very slowly, so it kept dumping wind, rain and high tides on the same area for a long time.

perspectives.description: Kenny Formica is worried because water came inside his marina, something that almost never happens — the last time was Hurricane Sandy.
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul warns that much more wind, rain and high tides are on the way, so people should be careful.
Forecasters explain that the storm moves very slowly, and that is exactly why it stays in one place and causes so much flooding.
